subject.title: Feature Request: Cross-platform migration tool (migrate export/import)

question: Should OpenClaw own an automated cross-platform import/restore command for local state, or keep restore user-driven while improving backup export/convert and documentation?
rationale: The requested workflow can write sensitive state from an archive into live config, credentials, sessions, and workspaces, and the prior same-feature PR already exposed maintainer disagreement about that security boundary.

options.title: Conservative backup/convert path
options.body: Extend `openclaw backup` with safer selective or platform-targeted export/convert behavior and document user-driven restore without automated writes into live state.

options.title: Approve automated import
options.body: Permit an import/restore command only with preview-first UX, archive trust warnings, canonical target validation, symlink-safe writes, rollback, and focused security tests.

options.title: Defer core migration work
options.body: Keep current manual migration guidance and revisit native export/import after backup and state storage hardening matures.

recommendation.title: Conservative backup/convert path
recommendation.body: Extend `openclaw backup` with safer selective or platform-targeted export/convert behavior and document user-driven restore without automated writes into live state.

likelyOwner.reason: They provided the clearest prior maintainer signal about the restore security boundary and have adjacent backup hardening history.
